rules.rule_en: Back-formation is the process of creating a new lexeme by removing actual or supposed affixes from longer words.
A blend word is a word formed from parts of two or more other words.
Clipped words are words that are formed by dropping one or more syllables from longer words without changing the meaning.
Clipping is a type of word formation where a word is reduced to a shorter form while retaining the same meaning.
Back-formation is the process of creating a new word (usually a verb) by removing an actual or supposed affix from another word (usually a noun).
Blended words are formed by combining parts of two or more words to create a new word.
Blending is the process of combining two words to form a new word.
Clipping is the process of shortening a longer word into a new word.
Clipping is the process of forming a new word by shortening a longer word, often retaining the meaning of the original word.
Singular nouns refer to one person, place, or thing, take a singular verb, and can be preceded by 'a' or 'an'.
Plural nouns refer to more than one person, place, or thing, take a plural verb, and are not preceded by 'a' or 'an'.
Many singular nouns form their plural by adding '-s'.
Singular forms ending with 'us' change into 'i'.
Some nouns become plural when we change the vowels.
Add 's' to the first word in hyphenated words.
Some nouns ending with 'o, s, ss, ch, sh, x, is' change into 'es'.
In compound nouns both elements get converted into plural forms.
Some nouns have two plural forms.
Compound nouns take 's' in plural form.
Singular forms ending with '-um' change into '-a'.
In case there is a vowel before 'y', just add 's' to form plural.
Nouns ending with 'f'/'fe' form their plural by changing into 'v' and adding 'es'.
Some nouns that end in 'o', you add 'es' or 's' to form the plural.
Some nouns do not change while taking plural form.
Some nouns have no singular form.
Singular forms ending with '-is' change into '-es'.
Nouns ending with '-y' form the plural by changing '-y' into '-i' and adding '-es'.
‘a’ ending in the singular forms changing into ‘ae’
Formation of plural nouns from singular forms using irregular suffix variations (e.g., -is to -es, -us to -i, -um to -a).
New words can be formed by a process called affixation, which involves adding affixes to the root word.
If an affix is attached to the beginning of a word, it is called a Prefix.
If an affix is attached to the end of a word, it is called a Suffix.
Words that are derived or formed from the base word by adding prefixes and suffixes are called derivatives.
Prefixes like 'un' and 'dis' are added to base words to form antonyms.
Suffix: A letter or a group of letters added at the end of a root word to make a different or a new form of the word. By adding suffixes, the meaning or grammatical function of a root word changes.
A prefix is a letter or group of letters added to the beginning of a root word to modify it, often creating an opposite.
A suffix is a letter or group of letters added to the end of a root word, changing its grammatical function.
Suffix: A letter or letters added at the end of a word to make a different or a new form of the word.
A blend word or a blend is a word formed from parts of two or more other words.
Derivatives are formed by adding prefixes or suffixes to a root word to change its grammatical form or meaning.
